title: Resentment leads techie to circulate fake obscene images of woman online

reading.body:
An AI image generation system was used to create fake obscene images of a real person without consent. The person obtained source photographs from the victim's social media, fed them to an AI system to generate explicit morphed images, and then distributed the results across multiple anonymous accounts. This represents a misuse of deployed AI technology to create and spread non-consensual intimate imagery.

The failure point was not in the AI system itself but in access control and the absence of friction between generation and distribution. Nothing in the summary indicates the AI system had safety measures to refuse the request, flag it, or require identity verification. The person was able to generate, download, and immediately circulate the images through platforms that accepted anonymous uploads.

It is not established what specific AI tools were used, whether they had built-in safeguards, or whether the platforms hosting the fake accounts were aware of the synthetic imagery. The investigation was conducted by law enforcement after the victim reported receiving messages about the content.

reports.title: Delhi: Man held for circulating obscene AI-generated photos of college acquaintance
Resentment leads techie to circulate fake obscene images of woman online

summary:
A 22-year-old man named Keshav Bansal was arrested in Delhi for creating and spreading obscene artificial intelligence-generated images of a college acquaintance. Bansal, a BTech graduate, obtained private photographs from the woman's social media account and used AI technology to create morphed explicit images. He then distributed this content through multiple fake Instagram, Discord, and Facebook accounts while using various Gmail addresses to hide his identity.

The victim, also 22 years old, discovered the harassment when she received messages from anonymous accounts informing her that her altered images were being shared on Discord servers. She reported the matter to the Cyber Police Station in North Delhi. During the investigation, police analyzed digital footprints and traced connections between the fake accounts. Bansal confessed that personal resentment toward the woman from college motivated his actions, though other online users later created additional explicit content that he reposted. Police recovered his mobile phone, SIM cards, and digital evidence as the investigation continues.
